title: Support explicit bucket boundaries (advisory parameters) when creating histograms
description:
The OpenTelemetry metrics API lets instrumentations pass [advisory parameters](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/v1.55.0/specification/metrics/api.md#instrument-advisory-parameters) when creating a histogram, in particular `ExplicitBucketBoundaries`. Several semantic conventions rely on this. For example the GenAI client inference conventions say `gen_ai.client.inference.duration` SHOULD use boundaries `[0.01, 0.02, 0.04, ..., 81.92]` and the token histograms `[1, 4, 16, ..., 67108864]`.

Currently `meter$create_histogram()` only accepts `name`, `description`, and `unit`:

```r
m <- otel::get_meter("x")
args(m$create_histogram)
#> function (name, description = NULL, unit = NULL)
```

so an instrumented package has no way to supply the advised boundaries and falls back to the SDK defaults. Would it be possible to add an argument such as `boundaries = NULL` (passed through to otelsdk as the explicit bucket boundaries advice)?

Context: tidyverse/ellmer#1143.

title: Add otel and otelsdk to the OpenTelemetry registry?
description:
The list of supported languages in OpenTelemetry's [Language APIs & SDKs page](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/) does not yet include R. From https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/other/:

> For some languages, unofficial implementations exist – you can find them in the [registry](https://opentelemetry.io/ecosystem/registry/). If you know about an implementation not listed there, please [add it to the registry](https://opentelemetry.io/ecosystem/registry/adding/).

title: No way to record a length-1 character vector as an array attribute
description:
Some semantic conventions define attributes as `string[]`, for example [`gen_ai.response.finish_reasons`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/docs/registry/attributes/gen-ai.md), which is usually a single value like `["stop"]`.

From R there is no way to express a one-element array:

```r
sp <- otel::start_span("x")
sp$set_attribute("a", "stop")          # recorded as a scalar string
sp$set_attribute("b", c("stop", "x"))  # recorded as a string array
sp$set_attribute("c", list("stop"))
#> Error: `value` must be of type character, logical, double, or integer, but it is a list.
```

So a length-1 vector always becomes a scalar, and consumers expecting `string[]` (array queries, schema checks, the Collector GenAI normalizer) see a different type than other instrumentations emit.

Would it be possible to support an explicit "this is an array" marker? For example honoring `I("stop")` (`AsIs`) or accepting a list of scalars, so that `set_attribute("a", I("stop"))` is exported as a one-element array.

Context: tidyverse/ellmer#1147.

title: Scopes from get_tracer(name) can't be matched by package name
description:
When a package passes its scope name to `get_tracer()`, `OTEL_R_SUPPRESS_SCOPES` and `OTEL_R_EMIT_SCOPES` can't match it by package name. This is still true after the fix for #50.

`default_tracer_name()` only looks up the calling package when `name` is `NULL`. If a name is given, it sets the package to `NA`:

```r
default_tracer_name <- function(name = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(name)) {
    ret <- list(name = name, package = NA_character_)
    ...
```

Tested with ellmer and otel 0.2.0.9000 (r-lib/otel@4d35f8b):

| | With name supplied | With no name supplied |
|---|---|---|
| `OTEL_R_SUPPRESS_SCOPES=ellmer` | doesn't work | works |
| `OTEL_R_SUPPRESS_SCOPES=co.posit.r-package.ellmer` | works | works |
| `OTEL_R_EMIT_SCOPES=ellmer` | ellmer is left out | works |

The last row is the worst case. A user who asks for only ellmer's telemetry gets nothing, with no warning.

Packages that set `otel_tracer_name` are split on this:

| Package | Call | Can `<package>` match it? |
|---|---|---|
| promises | `otel::get_tracer()` | Yes |
| shiny | `otel::get_tracer()` | Yes |
| mirai | `otel::get_tracer(otel_tracer_name)` | No |
| httr2 | `otel::get_tracer(otel_tracer_name)` | No |
| ellmer (before tidyverse/ellmer#1188) | `otel::get_tracer(otel_tracer_name)` | No |


Options:

1. **otel infers the package even when a name is given.** `default_tracer_name()` could walk the call stack in both cases and keep the given name. Then httr2, mirai, and others work with no changes.
2. **Packages should never pass their own name.** If so, it would help to say this in `?get_tracer` and `?default_tracer_name`, so that packages set `otel_tracer_name` and call `get_tracer()` with no arguments. We can then send PRs to httr2 and mirai.

The cost of not passing a name is small: a few microseconds per `get_tracer()` call. ellmer, httr2, and mirai cache the tracer in `.onLoad()`, so that happens once per session.

Related: #50, tidyverse/ellmer#1188.

title: OTEL_R_SUPPRESS_SCOPES needs both scope name and package name to match
description:
`OTEL_R_SUPPRESS_SCOPES` only turns a scope off when **both** its scope name and its package name match the list. A package that sets its own scope name can't be turned off by its package name alone. A package that passes a name to `get_tracer()` can't be turned off at all.

### Why

`is_scope_on()` filters `c(scope$name, scope$package)` and treats the scope as on if anything is left:

```r
flt <- glob_filter(c(scope$name, scope$package), inc, exc)
length(flt) > 0
```

- **Package with `otel_tracer_name` that calls `get_tracer()` with no name**: scope is `list(name = "co.posit.r-package.ellmer", package = "ellmer")`. `OTEL_R_SUPPRESS_SCOPES=ellmer` removes `"ellmer"` but leaves the scope name, so the scope stays on. Users must list both: `ellmer,co.posit.r-package.ellmer`.
- **Package that calls `get_tracer("some.name")`**: `default_tracer_name()` sets `package = NA_character_`. No pattern matches `NA`, so `glob_filter()` always returns it and the scope can never be suppressed, not even by its full name.

The docs say "a comma separated string of instrumentation scope names or R package names", so matching either one should be enough.

### Reprex

```r
library(otel) # 0.2.0, same logic on main

Sys.setenv(OTEL_R_SUPPRESS_SCOPES = "ellmer")
otel:::is_scope_on(list(name = "co.posit.r-package.ellmer", package = "ellmer"))
#> [1] TRUE   # expected FALSE

Sys.setenv(OTEL_R_SUPPRESS_SCOPES = "co.posit.r-package.ellmer")
otel:::default_tracer_name("co.posit.r-package.ellmer")$on
#> [1] TRUE   # expected FALSE

Sys.setenv(OTEL_R_SUPPRESS_SCOPES = "ellmer,co.posit.r-package.ellmer")
otel:::is_scope_on(list(name = "co.posit.r-package.ellmer", package = "ellmer"))
#> [1] FALSE
```

### Possible fix

Drop `NA` from the candidates, and turn the scope off if any candidate matches an exclude pattern. For `OTEL_R_EMIT_SCOPES`, keep it on if any candidate matches an include pattern. That is roughly what happens today, once the `NA` is dropped.

```r
candidates <- stats::na.omit(c(scope$name, scope$package))
if (!is.null(inc) && !any(glob_match(candidates, inc))) return(FALSE)
if (!is.null(exc) && any(glob_match(candidates, exc))) return(FALSE)
TRUE
```

Found while documenting ellmer's OpenTelemetry support (tidyverse/ellmer#1187).

title: Remove support for R expression in log messages
description:
The docs for the `otel_<severity>` functions say you can include R expressions in braces. This is dangerous. Here is a line from Shiny's `feat/otel` branch:

```
otel::log_info(paste0("Setting reactive values: ", key, " = ", value))
```

The `key` and `value` are both values sent by the client; a malicious visitor to this Shiny app could drop into the browser's JavaScript console and call `Shiny.setInputValue("bad", "{unlink("~", recursive=TRUE)}")`.

I suggest removing the R expression interpolation from the basic versions of `otel_<severity>` and add `otel_<severity>_glue` versions if you must. And even there, I suggest erroring if the first argument to `otel_<severity>_glue` is not a string literal.

title: Span `$add_link()` method
description:
According to https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/trace/api/#add-link:

> A Span MUST have the ability to add Links associated with it after its creation - see [Links](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/trace/api/#link). Links added after Span creation may not be considered by [Samplers](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/trace/sdk/#sampler).

also under https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/trace/api/#link:

> Span SHOULD preserve the order in which Links are set.

At the moment I'm working around this by adding events with the span ID as an attribute. This allows the span to be searched manually, but having an actual link would be more convenient in many UIs.

It might also be an option to add links to events as suggested here: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/issues/3337

```r
    otel::end_span(spn_c)
  }, add = TRUE)

  otel::with_active_span(spn_c, {
    spn_b <- otel::start_span("span_b", links = list(my_link = spn_a))
    Sys.sleep(0.1)
    otel::end_span(spn_b)
  })
})
```

Currently (when viewing with logfire), `span_a` and `span_c` are siblings ✅  and `span_b` is a child of `span_c` ✅ .
However, `span_b` has no concept of `span_a` in its raw data or within the UI ❌ .


Motivation... @atheriel had mentioned to me that spans should try to be small units of time. Shiny sessions can go for a very long time compared to the reactive graph locking / unlocking and its underlying computations. I was hoping to maybe link the reactive lock span to its session span. Similarly, I'd like to do this for initializing and resolving ExtendedTasks within Shiny.

title: Add `otel::local_span()`; Do not auto close `otel::start_span()`
description:
Bringing up the conversation again from https://github.com/r-lib/otel/issues/9#issuecomment-2998938541 . 

I'd really like to adjust `otel::start_span()` to perform no auto closing and add `otel::local_span()` which will behave as the current `otel::start_span()` does (ending on envir close). This gives us consistent `{withr}` style behavior.

With the adjustment, users would replace their current calls of `otel::start_span()` with `otel::local_span()`. No extra variables or lines of code are needed. And with the new function name it'll be understood to R users that there is automatic cleanup.

Python gets around the automatic ending as [they have a context manager](https://opentelemetry-python.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/trace.html#opentelemetry.trace.Tracer.start_span). Our conventions for context managers are the withr `local_FOO()` and `with_FOO()` syntax. [Go explicitly states](https://pkg.go.dev/go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace#Span) that it is "up to the operation the Span represents to end the Span" ([example](https://pkg.go.dev/go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace#section-documentation)). 

-------------------------

With `otel::start_span(name, tracer)`, calling `$end()` should be performed by the user. To safeguard it, would it be possible to add a finalizer that gives a message if the span has not be ended?

-------------------------

I could not find a clean solution for `otel::with_span()`. The closest I found would be https://github.com/r-lib/withr/blob/c8539fe735a5b6cdb496c68bca8248f8b6b4d419/R/tempfile.R#L22-L28 which I don't believe is a good solution. Having `otel::local_span()` should be sufficient.

title: Support for suppressing instrumentation for specific scopes
description:
Follow-up on https://github.com/r-lib/httr2/pull/729#pullrequestreview-2870995418.

I don't see anything in the OTel spec specifically for suppressing instrumentation from specific scopes (i.e. packages in our case), but I notice that [the Java implementation supports it](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/zero-code/java/agent/disable/#suppressing-specific-agent-instrumentation), as does [Logfire](https://logfire.pydantic.dev/docs/how-to-guides/suppress/).

We could have a [language-specific configuration extension](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/configuration/sdk-environment-variables/#language-specific-environment-variables) for this, e.g.

```
OTEL_R_SUPPRESS_SCOPES=httr2,ellmer
```

title: fix!: API for long running spans
description:
Problem: Current API uses the term `session` which is a heavily overloaded within Shiny, where many of the long running otel spans will be created.
* `otel::start_session()` 
* `otel::local_session()`
* `otel::with_session()`

Goal: Methods that maintain the `{withr}` style interface while signaling that the span will not be ended during / after the method completion.

-----------------

We had discussed before about using `otel::local_active_span(span)` and `otel::with_active_span(span, code)`, but the names could not be aligned with the constructor: `otel::start_span(auto_end = FALSE)`

After brain storming with @cpsievert, we came across "persistent_span" to describe a span that would not automatically close when the local environment ends.

This would lead to consistently named functions:
* `otel::start_persistent_span(name = NULL, tracer = NULL, ..., scope = parent.frame())` (which is a quick wrapper to `otel::start_span(name, tracer, ..., scope = scope, auto_end = FALSE)`)
* `otel::local_persistent_span(span, ..., .local_envir = parent.frame())`; (`...` are only used to separate `.local_envir`)
* `otel::with_persistent_span(span, code)`

----------------------

Continuing on the `{withr}` train, I'd like to propose that
* `otel::local_span(name = NULL, tracer = NULL, ..., .local_envir = parent.frame())` be a wrapper to `otel::start_span(..., scope = .local_envir, auto_end = TRUE)`
* `otel::with_span(name = NULL, code, tracer = NULL, ...)` which avoids users from writing `local({otel::local_span(name); my_code()})`. Instead could be `otel::with_span(name, my_code())`

I'm all about `local_FOO()` paired with `with_FOO()`. Users already understand that _local_ methods are reverted on context end and the _with_ methods are contained to only the code executed within. While, OTEL docs state that `start_span()` should be the entry point, `{otel}` can wrap that method with established R conventions.

title: Sessions without a parent trace might not work?
description:
Nevertheless this seems to work for me:
```r
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = "otel")

spn11 <- trc$start_span("11") # 1

trc$finish_session(sess1) # 1
```
